references.text: The ninth commandment forbids false testimony against your neighbor, which is the basis for the prohibition against spreading false rumors.
Prohibition against going about with gossip and standing against your neighbor's blood, expanding on the theme of false speech.
Repetition of the ninth commandment in Deuteronomy regarding false testimony.
Laws concerning false witnesses and the consequences of giving false testimony.
Blessed is the one who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, parallel to the warning against associating with evil people.
Description of false witnesses who come forward and accuse others for what they do not know.
Warning against associating with someone who is quick to anger, related to not cooperating with the wicked.
Prohibition against being a witness against your neighbor without cause or deceiving with one's lips.
False witnesses sought testimony against Jesus, fulfilling the warning against false witnesses.
Exhortation to put away falsehood and speak truthfully with your neighbor.
Warning against having fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, parallel to not cooperating with the wicked.
Connected legal text: Verse 7 expands on the consequences of false accusations in the same chapter as verse 1.
Consequence perspective: Proverbs confirm that God's justice punishes the false witness whom the law warns against.
Repetition of consequence: Confirms that the liar will not escape God's judgment, consistent with the law in Exodus.
Character definition: Defines the contrast between truth and falsehood that underlies the law's requirements.
